title: Khirbet Qumran settlement, excavated remains (Magen & Peleg 2018, Fig. 9)

frame.origin: Centre of the round cistern L110: circle fitted to the inner face of its drawn ring on Fig. 9 (page-image pixel 563.96, 658.45)
frame.north: Fig. 9 north arrow, vertical on the page (grid or true north not stated)
frame.groundBasis: No level is used. Magen & Peleg print spot levels in metres below sea level on their detailed plans (e.g. Figs. 57, 41, 104), but Fig. 9 has none and the surface each spot marks is not stated; published pool depths are kept in height.value.

sources.citation: Magen & Peleg 2018, Back to Qumran: Final Report (1993-2004), Site Description, Fig. 9 'Qumran, general plan', printed p. 12 (full-report PDF p. 35)
sources.licence: CC BY-NC 4.0 per the JSTOR cover of the Site Description chapter (https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctv1t8cdq.6), as recorded in research/assets/plans/magen-peleg2018/README.md; attribute Yitzhak Magen and Yuval Peleg. The page-image manifest itself asserts no open licence.
sources.transform: frame = (px - p0) / 7.965, no rotation; p0 = (563.96, 658.45) px; 7.965 px per metre = 159.3 px for the 0-20 bar (0-10: 80.0 px, 10-20: 79.3 px) on the 2 px/pt page image
sources.residual: The bar is labelled '0 10 20 cm' but is 28.1 mm long on the page, so 'cm' cannot be a printed length; read as metres. Long sizes of 11 rooms and pools with drawn ends agree with published sizes at 0.99 +/- 0.02 (range 0.97-1.03), e.g. hall L77 21.91 m against 22.20 m (M&P p. 44) and pool L71 18.25-19.07 m against 19.10 m (M&P p. 90). Clear widths come out c. 0.1-0.5 m short because the walls are drawn with a heavy fill (see verification).

elements.label: Walls drawn filled (solid) on Fig. 9
elements.note: Threshold of the grey fill (grey < 128 of 255) on the 2 px/pt page image, 3 x 3 px opening (0.38 m) to remove text, thin lines and hatching, bold labels, caption, scale bar, north arrow and frame masked first; components under 15 px dropped; one 38 px dash piece of the dashed line west of L138 removed; L75's drawn outline removed (given as element L75-platform). Resampled to 0.25 m cells (cell set when at least half its area is wall). Includes the ring wall of cistern L110 and small filled squares such as the piers in L86-L89. Fig. 9 draws walls with a heavy fill: wall centre lines agree with published sizes, but faces stand c. 0.1-0.25 m proud of the true faces, so clear widths inside rooms and pools come out short (see verification). Walls drawn only as unfilled outlines are not in this raster (see limits). Preserved wall heights are not given by the plan.

elements.label: Channel: Aqueduct (labelled on Fig. 9)
elements.note: Width = centre-to-centre spacing of the two drawn lines (median of 87 profiles). Labelled 'Aqueduct' on Fig. 9. The authors' summary (M&P p. 90) gives a narrow phase A aqueduct to cistern L110 and a wide phase B aqueduct; which drawn line belongs to which phase is not marked on Fig. 9.

elements.label: Channel: double line from the aqueduct end south-east to the north-south channel
elements.note: Width = centre-to-centre spacing of the two drawn lines (median of 22 profiles). Thin double line read as a channel; no legend on Fig. 9.

elements.label: Channel: north-south channel drawn with side walls, from the aqueduct junction to W of L118
elements.note: Drawn with four parallel lines (spacing c. 0.5 / 0.4 / 0.5 m): read here as a channel with its two side walls, as Fig. 57 draws channel M5 at this place (stone side walls with the channel between). Width = outer lines; the inner (water) width between the middle lines is c. 0.52 m.

elements.label: Channel: channel continuing south past L116/L115 and round the east side of L110
elements.note: Traced by hand: the lines pass under the white label boxes of L116, L115 and L118 and round the east side of L110 (Galor p. 260: the channel circumscribes the eastern half of L110 and opens from the south). Width not measurable here (null).

elements.label: Channel: main channel south-east from L110 to L83
elements.note: Drawn with four parallel lines (spacings c. 0.36 / 0.24 / 0.49 m), not symmetric; Fig. 9 has no legend to say whether these are side walls or two superposed channels (M&P p. 80 reports two channels one above the other near L110). Width = outer lines.

elements.label: Channel: channel east from L83 to the west end of L56
elements.note: Width = centre-to-centre spacing of the two drawn lines (median of 23 profiles). From L83 east to the west end of L56 (M&P pp. 43-44: the channel from sedimentation pool L83 flowed into pool L56).

elements.label: Channel: channel south from the south-east corner of the L56/L58 block past L72 and south-east to L69
elements.note: Width = centre-to-centre spacing of the two drawn lines (median of 34 profiles). Runs south past L72 and south-east to L69 (M&P p. 90: the central channel entered L69 from the west).

elements.label: Channel: channel round L75 and south along the west side of L71
elements.note: Width = centre-to-centre spacing of the two drawn lines (median of 43 profiles). Starts at the round basin of L75 and runs south along the west side of L71 to the south end of the plan area; the fan of lines at its south end is not traced.

elements.label: Channel: channel from the L117 area north to the Northern Refuse Dump
elements.note: Width = centre-to-centre spacing of the two drawn lines (median of 125 profiles). Runs north from the north end of L117 to the Northern Refuse Dump; at its north end Fig. 9 draws three to four lines. Matches the covered overflow at the west side of the northern dump associated with L117 in the project record research/sources/qumran_northern_dump_contact_test_2026-10-02.md (identification by position only).

elements.label: Channel: channel from the L113 side west to the escarpment edge
elements.note: Width = centre-to-centre spacing of the two drawn lines (median of 30 profiles). Runs west to the escarpment edge. M&P p. 52: de Vaux associates the lower floor of L113 with the runoff channel from cistern L110 to the wadi on the west (match by position only).

elements.note: Width = centre-to-centre spacing of the two drawn lines (median of 113 profiles). Along the south edge of the Paved Square. M&P p. 46: the square is bounded on the south along its entire length by the 0.25 m-wide unplastered channel 18, which runs from the square's west to its south-east (match by position; traced line spacing 0.35 m centre to centre).

elements.label: L110 (round cistern)

levels.source: Fig. 57 (p. 53) prints -330.19 inside L110 and Fig. 58 section 2-2 (p. 54) shows the bottom near -330; the surface the spot marks is not stated and no rim level is given, so no level is used.

elements.locator: Magen & Peleg 2018, Fig. 9, printed p. 12; circle fitted to the inner face of the drawn ring
elements.note: Round cistern (M&P pp. 52, 56); it has no steps (Magness 2021 p. 181, project extract). Radius = inner face of the drawn ring (diameter 4.62 m on Fig. 9); the ring wall itself (0.94 m thick, outer diameter 6.53 m) is in walls-filled. Published: diameter 5.10 m (Galor p. 259); original wall 0.95 m thick (M&P p. 52). Fig. 57 at its own scale gives an inner diameter of c. 4.8-5.0 m. Raised in phase B (M&P p. 94).

elements.label: L85 (steps into L91)
elements.locator: Magen & Peleg 2018, Fig. 9, printed p. 12; the small hatched chamber at the north end of L91 to which the L85 label leader points
elements.note: Galor p. 262: four steps lead from north to south to a basin (1.7 x 1.7 m) that opens on pool L91; Magness 2021 p. 182 (project extract): 'L85 is not a pool but rather steps' into L91. Interior traced 1.8 x 2.8 m.

elements.label: Escarpment line with ticks, west and south-west of the site
elements.note: Line with short ticks. The ticks lie on the inner (south-west) side of the northern arc and on the west side of the long southern run; by the usual hachure convention that side is lower (towards the wadi west of the Western Structure, M&P p. 51), but Fig. 9 gives no legend.

elements.label: U-shaped escarpment line with ticks, north of the site
elements.note: Ticks on the inside (north) of the U; by the hachure convention the inside is lower (a gully opening to the north). No legend on Fig. 9. The line runs to the frame edge.

elements.label: Outline drawn round the north-west tower (west, north and east sides)
elements.note: Thin outer line with lighter inner lines round the tower. M&P p. 15: inclined retaining walls and a stone glacis (W509, W510) were added to the tower's faces. Fig. 9 gives only the outline, no slope or height; traced by hand (+/- 2 px, 0.25 m).

features.description: At the edge of the site above the wadi on its west; an addition to the central structure, separated from it by a courtyard that included the water system.

features.label: Main Building
features.description: Square structure on the north of the plateau with rooms and halls round a central courtyard; two towers on the north.

Preserved wall heights and absolute levels are not traced; pool depths are published depths below an unknown rim (height.value).

Fig. 9 is the 2018 report's general plan of all excavated remains; it does not separate phases (the authors' phases A and B, de Vaux's periods) and has no legend for dashed lines, double lines, hatching or ticks.

Walls drawn only as unfilled outlines (thin double lines), chiefly in the central courtyard of the Main Building (around L24, L37, L34), west of L30 and in the north-east wing (L41, L39), are not traced in this version; Fig. 41 (p. 39) draws the courtyard ones as stone walls (e.g. W547, W563, W566, W567).

Single thin lines of unstated meaning are not traced: the outline round the west side of the Western Structure, the loop south-east of L113, the lighter inner lines round the north-west tower, the fan of lines south of L71 and small marks at L64.
Channel lines under the white label boxes of L116, L115 and L118 and inside the dense junctions near L138 and L110 are read by hand to c. +/- 2 px (0.25 m).
Heavy wall fill: clear widths inside rooms and pools are c. 0.1-0.5 m short; L83's outline is not separable from L85 at this scale.
Pool functions are the sources' words (e.g. 'sedimentation pool' is Magen & Peleg's interpretation); the tracing adds no function.
